title: Phishing & Social Engineering Risk Calculator
metaDescription: Calculate your vulnerability to phishing attacks and social engineering tactics. Get personalized security recommendations to protect yourself.
description: Assess your personal risk level for phishing scams and social engineering attacks. This calculator evaluates your current security practices and provides actionable recommendations to strengthen your defenses against cybercriminals.

inputs.label: How do you typically handle suspicious emails?

options.label: Click links immediately if they look legitimate
Never click links, always navigate manually

inputs.helpText: Your email behavior is the primary defense against phishing attacks

inputs.label: How do you manage your passwords?

options.label: Use the same password for most accounts
Use a password manager with unique passwords

inputs.helpText: Password reuse significantly increases your risk if one account is compromised

inputs.label: Do you use two-factor authentication (2FA)?

options.label: On all accounts that support it

inputs.helpText: 2FA provides an additional security layer even if passwords are compromised

inputs.label: How much personal information do you share on social media?

options.label: Share personal details, location, family info regularly
Share some personal info but limit sensitive details
Don't use social media or share nothing personal

inputs.helpText: Oversharing helps attackers craft convincing personalized attacks

inputs.label: How frequently do you update your software and browsers?
inputs.helpText: Outdated software contains security vulnerabilities that attackers exploit

inputs.label: How often do you use public WiFi for sensitive activities?

options.label: Often use public WiFi for banking, shopping, etc.
Never use public WiFi for anything sensitive

inputs.helpText: Public WiFi networks are often monitored by cybercriminals

inputs.label: How well do you recognize phishing attempts?

options.label: I often can't tell if emails are legitimate
I can spot obvious scams but sophisticated ones fool me
I can identify most phishing attempts
I'm very skilled at recognizing all types of attacks

inputs.helpText: Knowledge of attack techniques is your best defense

outputFields.label: Overall Risk Score
outputFields.description: Your total vulnerability score out of 100

outputFields.label: Attack Success Probability
outputFields.description: Estimated likelihood of falling victim to a targeted attack

formula: const weights = { emailHabits: 25, passwordPractices: 20, twoFactorAuth: 15, socialMediaSharing: 10, softwareUpdates: 10, publicWifiUsage: 10, securityAwareness: 10 }; const scores = { emailHabits: { 'click-immediately': 100, 'sometimes-verify': 70, 'check-sender': 30, 'never-click': 10 }, passwordPractices: { 'same-everywhere': 100, 'few-variations': 75, 'some-unique': 50, 'all-unique': 25, 'password-manager': 5 }, twoFactorAuth: { 'never': 100, 'some-accounts': 60, 'most-accounts': 30, 'all-accounts': 10 }, socialMediaSharing: { 'everything': 100, 'moderate': 60, 'minimal': 30, 'none': 10 }, softwareUpdates: { 'rarely': 100, 'monthly': 60, 'weekly': 30, 'automatic': 10 }, publicWifiUsage: { 'frequently': 100, 'sometimes': 60, 'rarely': 30, 'never': 10 }, securityAwareness: { 'poor': 100, 'somewhat': 60, 'good': 30, 'excellent': 10 } }; let totalScore = 0; Object.keys(weights).forEach(key => { totalScore += (scores[key][inputs[key]] * weights[key]) / 100; }); const riskScore = Math.round(totalScore); let riskLevel, vulnerabilityPercentage; if (riskScore <= 25) { riskLevel = 'A+'; vulnerabilityPercentage = 5; } else if (riskScore <= 35) { riskLevel = 'A'; vulnerabilityPercentage = 15; } else if (riskScore <= 50) { riskLevel = 'B'; vulnerabilityPercentage = 30; } else if (riskScore <= 65) { riskLevel = 'C'; vulnerabilityPercentage = 55; } else if (riskScore <= 80) { riskLevel = 'D'; vulnerabilityPercentage = 75; } else { riskLevel = 'F'; vulnerabilityPercentage = 90; } return { riskScore, riskLevel, vulnerabilityPercentage };

educational.methodology: This calculator evaluates seven key factors that determine your vulnerability to phishing and social engineering attacks. Each factor is weighted based on its importance in real-world attack scenarios, with email habits being the most critical factor since email is the primary attack vector.
tips: Always verify the sender's email address by hovering over it before clicking any links
Use a password manager to generate and store unique passwords for every account
Enable two-factor authentication on all accounts that support it, especially financial and email accounts
Keep your browser, operating system, and security software updated automatically
Use Incognito Browser for enhanced privacy protection when browsing suspicious links
Be skeptical of urgent requests for personal information, even from seemingly trusted sources
Limit personal information sharing on social media to reduce targeted attack opportunities
Never enter sensitive information when connected to public WiFi networks
Verify requests through a separate communication channel when in doubt

interpretation.label: Excellent Security (A+)
interpretation.description: You have strong defenses against phishing and social engineering attacks. Continue following security best practices and stay updated on new threats.

interpretation.label: Very Good Security (A)
interpretation.description: You're well-protected but there's room for minor improvements. Consider strengthening your weakest security areas.

interpretation.label: Good Security (B)
interpretation.description: You have decent protection but should address several security gaps to improve your defenses against sophisticated attacks.

interpretation.label: Fair Security (C)
interpretation.description: You're moderately vulnerable to attacks. Focus on improving password practices, enabling 2FA, and being more cautious with emails.

interpretation.label: Poor Security (D)
interpretation.description: You're at high risk of falling victim to phishing attacks. Immediate action is needed to improve your security practices.

interpretation.label: Very Poor Security (F)
interpretation.description: You're extremely vulnerable to attacks. Urgent security improvements are essential to protect yourself from cybercriminals.
